intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that retinitis pigmentosa-56 (RP56) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the IMPG2 gene (607056) on chromosome 3q12.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa-56 (RP56) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the IMPG2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis of IMPG2 in the two index cases revealed homozygous mutations cosegregating with the disease in the respective families
checks.explanation: Abstract reports homozygous IMPG2 mutations causing arRP; compound heterozygosity is not mentioned.

checks.claim: The IMPG2 gene is located on chromosome 3q12.
checks.evidence_quote: large overlapping homozygous regions that harbored the IMPG2 gene on chromosome 3
checks.explanation: Abstract states chromosome 3; the 3q12 band is standard location nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Retinitis pigmentosa-56 (RP56) is an autosomal recessive form of retinitis pigmentosa, a progressive degeneration of the retina in which rod photoreceptors are mainly affected first. Patients have night blindness and progressive loss of peripheral vision, and the macula may also be involved.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa-56 (RP56) is an autosomal recessive form of retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in IMPG2, encoding interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan 2, cause autosomal-recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.explanation: IMPG2-related RP is autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa is a progressive degeneration of the retina in which rod photoreceptors are mainly affected first.
checks.evidence_quote: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a heterogeneous group of inherited retinal diseases caused by progressive degeneration of the photoreceptor cells.
checks.explanation: Progressive photoreceptor degeneration is stated, but the abstract does not say rods are affected first.

checks.claim: Patients with RP56 have night blindness.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention night blindness. It may be in the full text, but only the abstract was supplied.

checks.claim: Patients with RP56 have progressive loss of peripheral vision.
checks.evidence_quote: Most patients with IMPG2 mutations showed an early-onset form of RP with progressive visual-field loss and deterioration of visual acuity.
checks.explanation: Progressive visual-field loss corresponds to loss of peripheral vision.

checks.claim: The macula may be involved in patients with RP56.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient with the missense mutation, however, was diagnosed with maculopathy.
checks.explanation: Only one patient is reported with maculopathy, and that patient was diagnosed with maculopathy rather than RP.

paragraphs.text: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) studied several families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa. Affected individuals had night blindness and constriction of the visual field, with fundus findings typical of RP, including bone spicule pigmentation and attenuated retinal vessels. Macular involvement was also seen in some patients.

checks.claim: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) studied several families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: Using autozygosity mapping, we identified two families, each with three affected siblings sharing large overlapping homozygous regions that harbored the IMPG2 gene on chromosome 3.
checks.explanation: The paper studied two families plus ten additional index cases with arRP.

checks.claim: Individuals affected with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa in the families studied by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) had night blindness.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention night blindness. It may be in the full text, but only the abstract was supplied.

checks.claim: Individuals affected with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa in the families studied by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) had constriction of the visual field.
checks.evidence_quote: Most patients with IMPG2 mutations showed an early-onset form of RP with progressive visual-field loss and deterioration of visual acuity.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports visual-field loss in most patients, which is close to but not the same as visual-field constriction in all affected individuals.

checks.claim: Individuals affected with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa in the families studied by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) had bone spicule pigmentation on fundus examination.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not describe bone spicule pigmentation or other fundus findings.

checks.claim: Individuals affected with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa in the families studied by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) had attenuated retinal vessels on fundus examination.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention attenuated retinal vessels.

checks.claim: Some patients with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa in the families studied by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) had macular involvement.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient with the missense mutation, however, was diagnosed with maculopathy.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports maculopathy in a single patient who was diagnosed with maculopathy rather than RP, not macular involvement in some RP patients.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of RP56 in the families reported by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of RP56 in the families reported by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis of IMPG2 in the two index cases revealed homozygous mutations cosegregating with the disease in the respective families
checks.explanation: Homozygous mutations cosegregating in sibships fit autosomal recessive inheritance, and the title states arRP.

paragraphs.text: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) used homozygosity mapping in families with autosomal recessive RP and identified a homozygous region on chromosome 3q that contained the IMPG2 gene.

checks.claim: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) used homozygosity mapping in families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: Using autozygosity mapping, we identified two families, each with three affected siblings sharing large overlapping homozygous regions
checks.explanation: Autozygosity mapping is homozygosity mapping.

checks.claim: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) identified a homozygous region on chromosome 3q containing the IMPG2 gene in families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: sharing large overlapping homozygous regions that harbored the IMPG2 gene on chromosome 3
checks.explanation: The abstract says chromosome 3; the 3q arm is standard location for IMPG2.

paragraphs.text: Heterozygous mutations in the IMPG2 gene have also been reported to cause a distinct, dominantly inherited phenotype, vitelliform macular dystrophy.

checks.claim: Heterozygous mutations in the IMPG2 gene have been reported to cause vitelliform macular dystrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: With an autosomal dominant transmission, families 1 and 2 had the c.713T→G (p.Leu238Arg) mutation in IMPG1 and family 4 had the c.3230G→T (p.Cys1077Phe) mutation in IMPG2.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports an IMPG2 mutation causing vitelliform macular dystrophy with autosomal dominant transmission, which implies a heterozygous mutation. The abstract does not use the word 'heterozygous'.

checks.claim: Vitelliform macular dystrophy caused by heterozygous IMPG2 mutations is a dominantly inherited phenotype distinct from RP56.
checks.evidence_quote: With an autosomal dominant transmission, families 1 and 2 had the c.713T→G (p.Leu238Arg) mutation in IMPG1 and family 4 had the c.3230G→T (p.Cys1077Phe) mutation in IMPG2.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports dominant inheritance of IMPG2-related vitelliform macular dystrophy. It does not compare this phenotype with RP56 or call it distinct from RP56.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa, Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) found homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the IMPG2 gene. IMPG2 encodes interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan-2, a part of the interphotoreceptor matrix that surrounds the photoreceptor outer segments. Most of the mutations were predicted to truncate the protein, and the mutations segregated with the disease in the families.

checks.claim: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) found homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the IMPG2 gene in affected members of families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis of IMPG2 in the two index cases revealed homozygous mutations cosegregating with the disease in the respective families
checks.explanation: Only homozygous mutations are reported; compound heterozygous mutations are not mentioned.

checks.claim: IMPG2 encodes interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan-2.
checks.evidence_quote: The IMPG2 gene encodes the interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan IMPG2, which is a constituent of the interphotoreceptor matrix.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan-2 is a part of the interphotoreceptor matrix that surrounds the photoreceptor outer segments.
checks.evidence_quote: The IMPG2 gene encodes the interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan IMPG2, which is a constituent of the interphotoreceptor matrix.
checks.explanation: The abstract says IMPG2 is part of the interphotoreceptor matrix but does not say the matrix surrounds photoreceptor outer segments.

checks.claim: Most of the IMPG2 mutations identified by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) were predicted to truncate the protein.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed five additional mutations; four nonsense mutations and one missense mutation
checks.explanation: Five of the seven mutations are nonsense mutations, which are expected to truncate the protein. The other two are an in-frame exon deletion and a missense mutation.

checks.claim: The IMPG2 mutations identified by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) segregated with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa in the families.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed homozygous mutations cosegregating with the disease in the respective families
checks.explanation: Cosegregation is stated for the two index families.
